Occupancy family for repeated detection and non-detection

Source: R/families.R
occ.Rd

For detections recorded on repeated visits to sites whose occupancy stays fixed across the visits, such as camera-trap or call surveys within a season. The data hold one row per visit with a 0 / 1 response. The visits sharing a series and a time belong to one closure unit, which is occupied with probability mu. A visit to an occupied unit detects the species with probability p. The likelihood sums over the unit's two states. A unit with a detection is occupied for certain (MacKenzie et al. 2002).

Usage

occ(multi_season = FALSE)

Arguments

multi_season

Logical. TRUE keys a closure unit on (series, site, time), for several seasons of visits to each site. The data then need a site column, which pivot_detection_array() creates from a four-dimensional array with multi_season = "hierarchical". Each unit holds the visits of one site in one season.

Value

A family object to pass to mvgam() or jsdgam().

Details

bf(y ~ elev, p ~ tod) models occupancy and detection, each with its own formula on the logit link. predict() with type = "latent_state" gives the probability that each unit is occupied given its detections. type = "detection" gives the detection probability of each visit. The data need no cap column.

Priors

The occupancy intercept takes brms's student_t(3, 0, 2.5) on the logit scale. A scalar p takes beta(1, 1). With a formula, its intercept takes normal(0, 1.5). get_prior() lists the defaults, and prior(..., dpar = "p") replaces one.

Identification

The detections identify occupancy and detection apart through repeated visits and through covariates that act on one of them. With one visit per unit and no covariate, the data identify only the product mu * p. Only the priors then set the two apart (Royle and Dorazio 2008). mvgam() warns on such data. It also warns when more than 30% of units have a single visit.

Joint species models

jsdgam() with nmix() or occ() fits several species at once. Latent factors shared by the species enter the state mu. p keeps its own formula. factor_formula = ~ s(env, by = lv_axis()) lets each factor follow an environmental gradient.

Importing array data

Detection histories from unmarked, spOccupancy or ubms come as a site-by-visit matrix, an array with species or seasons as further dimensions, or a list of matrices. pivot_detection_array() converts any of these to the long format, broadcasting site, season and visit covariates to their rows.

Threading

The density sums over units through Stan's reduce_sum(). Fitting with threads = 2 or more splits the units across threads.

References

MacKenzie, D. I., Nichols, J. D., Lachman, G. B., Droege, S., Royle, J. A. and Langtimm, C. A. (2002). Estimating site occupancy rates when detection probabilities are less than one. Ecology, 83, 2248-2255. doi:10.1890/0012-9658(2002)083[2248:ESORWD]2.0.CO;2

Royle, J. A. and Dorazio, R. M. (2008). Hierarchical Modeling and Inference in Ecology. Academic Press.

See also

nmix() for the related N-mixture family and pp_check.mvgam() for closure-unit goodness-of-fit checks. The N-mixture article fits occupancy and N-mixture models from data preparation to inference. The data article sets out the row layout that occ() expects.

Other observation families: beta_nb(), categ(), com_binomial(), diri(), multi(), mvgam_families, mvn(), mvt(), nmix(), tweedie()

Examples

# \dontrun{
# Detections at 50 sites, each visited four times, with covariates
# on occupancy and on detection
set.seed(6)
simdat <- sim_closure_unit_data(family = occ(), n_species = 1L,
                                n_sites = 50L, n_visits = 4L,
                                type = 1L)
mod <- mvgam(
  bf(y ~ env, p ~ tod_c),
  data   = simdat$data_train,
  family = occ(),
  chains = 2,
  silent = 2
)
summary(mod)
#>  Family: occ 
#>   Links: mu = logit; p = logit 
#> Formula: y ~ env 
#>          p ~ tod_c 
#>    Data: simdat$data_train (Number of observations: 200) 
#>   Draws: 2 chains, each with iter = 2000; warmup = 1000; thin = 1; 
#>          total post-warmup draws = 2000
#> 
#> == Observation Model ==
#> Regression Coefficients:
#>             Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS
#> Intercept       0.57      0.55    -0.39     1.93 1.00     1538      656
#> p_Intercept     0.20      0.25    -0.29     0.67 1.00     1802     1415
#> env            -3.39      1.33    -6.73    -1.53 1.00     1323      684
#> p_tod_c        -0.32      0.07    -0.46    -0.19 1.00     1557     1235
#> 
#> Draws were sampled using sampling(NUTS). For each parameter, Bulk_ESS
#> and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential
#> scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1).
#> 
#> Next steps:
#>   - `pp_check(fit, type = "fit_stat")`: goodness of fit of unit totals
#>   - `plot(hindcast(fit, type = "latent_state"))`: posterior occupancy of each unit
#>   - `forecast(fit, newdata = ...)`: out-of-sample forecasts
#>   - `loo(fit)` / `loo_compare(...)`: model fit + comparison
#>   - `conditional_effects(fit)`: covariate effects
#> Use `how_to_cite(fit)` for a methods paragraph and `methods_md(fit)` for its equations.

# Occupancy along the gradient and detection through the day
conditional_effects(mod, effects = "env", type = "latent_state")

conditional_effects(mod, effects = "tod_c", type = "detection")


# Occupancy and detection, separated by the model
head(predict(mod, type = "latent_state"))
#>          Estimate   Est.Error         Q2.5       Q97.5
